Definition: properly, deputyship, i.e. ministry; generally, employment (never servile) or work (abstractly or concretely); also property (as the result of labor)
BiblicalUsage: Mela'kah is work in the widest sense: employment, business, ministry, and the thing made by labour. Genesis 2:2 says God ended His work which He had made and rested on the seventh day, and Exodus 20:9 commands six days of labour to do all our work. Exodus 31:3 shows the other side, where God fills Bezalel with His Spirit for all manner of workmanship, and 1 Kings 5:16 sets officers over Solomon's workmen.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe work began with God, not with the fall: He worked first, and He rested, and He still gives skill for the work He asks of us. My position is that ordinary labour is holy when it is done as service to Him, whether it is building a temple or earning a living.
